A.explanation: Acceleration has units of $\text{m s}^{-2}$, which cannot be rearranged to give $\text{N s}^2 \text{m}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Force has units of $\text{N}$, equivalent to $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, so it has an extra $\text{m s}^{-2}$ compared with the given combination.

C.explanation: Expanding $\text{N}$ as $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{s}^2 \times \text{m}^{-1} = \text{kg}$, the SI unit of mass.

D.explanation: Momentum has units of $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, equivalent to $\text{N s}$, which lacks one factor of $\text{s m}^{-1}$.

walkthrough: Start from the definition of the newton from $F = ma$: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg} \times 1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Substitute this into the given units: $1 \text{ N s}^2 \text{ m}^{-1} = (1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}) \times (1 \text{ s}^2) \times (1 \text{ m}^{-1})$.
The base SI unit $\text{kg}$ is the unit of mass, and checking the list shows mass matches this result. This is option C
